name: com.growthbusinessfinance/mcp
title: Growth Business Finance
description: UK business finance: facility types, indicative sizes and an enquiry to a broker.

tools.name: find_facility_types
tools.description: Use this when a user describes a business funding need and wants to know which types of business finance could fit. Takes a description of the business and the need, and returns up to four matching facility types (for example invoice finance, asset based lending, a term loan, bridging or development finance), why each fits, what lenders usually look at, documents to prepare and indicative terms as published on growthbusinessfinance.com. If the user asks for a facility type by name, pass it in interested_in so it is shown first. The order of the results is not a ranking. Results are general information from Growth Business Finance, a UK commercial finance broker: not advice and not an offer of finance.

business_description.description: What the business does, in a sentence or two.

sector.description: The business's sector, for example manufacturing or recruitment.

uk_based.description: True if the business is based in the UK.

trading_years.description: Years the business has been trading, or null if unknown.

profitable.description: Whether the business is currently profitable.

assets.description: Assets the business holds that could support lending. Use ['none'] if none.

amount_band.description: Roughly how much funding is needed.

interested_in.description: Facility types the user has asked for by name, if any (for example cash_flow_term_loan when they ask for a cash flow loan). They are shown first.

tools.name: explain_facility
tools.description: Use this when a user asks how one type of business finance works. Returns a summary, how it works, typical uses, who it suits, what lenders usually look at and indicative terms for the chosen facility type, taken from growthbusinessfinance.com. General information, not advice.

tools.name: estimate_size
tools.description: Use this when a user wants a rough idea of how much a facility type could raise against a figure they know, such as their debtor book, stock value, asset cost, property value or EBITDA. Applies only the advance rates and loan-to-value figures published on growthbusinessfinance.com and returns an indicative amount with its source page. Always indicative and subject to lender assessment; if the website publishes no figure for that facility type, it says so instead of estimating.

debtor_book.description: The value of the debtor book (unpaid customer invoices), in pounds, if it applies to this facility type.

stock_value.description: The value of stock, in pounds, if it applies to this facility type.

plant_machinery_value.description: The value of plant and machinery, in pounds, if it applies to this facility type.

property_value.description: The value of the property, in pounds, if it applies to this facility type.

asset_cost.description: The cost of the asset being bought, in pounds, if it applies to this facility type.

supplier_cost.description: The cost of the goods being bought from suppliers, in pounds, if it applies to this facility type.

gross_development_value.description: The gross development value of the scheme, in pounds, if it applies to this facility type.

total_development_cost.description: The total cost of the development, in pounds, if it applies to this facility type.

annual_ebitda.description: Annual EBITDA, in pounds, if it applies to this facility type.

annual_recurring_revenue.description: Annual recurring revenue, in pounds, if it applies to this facility type.

tools.name: example_deals
tools.description: Use this when a user asks for examples of business finance deals. Returns up to three anonymous, published stories of completed deals that Growth Business Finance arranged, optionally filtered by facility type or sector. They are a selection, with no client or lender names.

facility_type.description: Only show deals involving this facility type.

sector.description: Only show deals in this sector.

tools.name: submit_enquiry
tools.description: Use this only when the user asks to send an enquiry to Growth Business Finance, a UK commercial finance broker. It sends the user's business, funding need and contact details to GBF, where a human broker reviews it, and returns a reference and the next steps. Before calling: show the user a summary of everything that will be sent and get their explicit confirmation, and get their explicit agreement to be contacted by GBF and to GBF's privacy notice (https://growthbusinessfinance.com/privacy-policy/). Set the two consent fields to true only if the user has agreed. If the reply lists several companies, ask the user which is theirs and call again with its company_number. Repeating a call with the same details does not create a second enquiry.

business_description.description: What the business does, in a sentence or two.

sector.description: The business's sector, for example manufacturing or recruitment.

uk_based.description: True if the business is based in the UK.

trading_years.description: Years the business has been trading, or null if unknown.

profitable.description: Whether the business is currently profitable.

assets.description: Assets the business holds that could support lending. Use ['none'] if none.

role.description: The user's role in the business, for example Finance Director.

amount_gbp.description: The amount of funding wanted, in pounds.

purpose_detail.description: Anything else the user wants GBF to know about the funding need.

consent_contact.description: True only if the user has explicitly agreed to be contacted by Growth Business Finance about this enquiry.

consent_privacy.description: True only if the user has explicitly agreed to GBF's privacy notice at https://growthbusinessfinance.com/privacy-policy/.

tools.name: get_available_slots
tools.description: Use this after submit_enquiry returns a booking_token and the user wants to book a call with Growth Business Finance. Returns up to six free 30 minute slots from the broker's calendar over the next two weeks, in the user's time zone and in UK time. It only reads availability and books nothing. Without a valid booking_token it says the broker will email to arrange a time instead.

booking_token.description: The booking_token returned by submit_enquiry. Never ask the user for it.

preferred_days.description: Weekdays the user prefers, if they said.

timezone.description: The user's IANA time zone, for example Europe/London. Defaults to UK time.

tools.name: book_call
tools.description: Use this only when the user has chosen one of the slots from get_available_slots and asked to book it. It books a 30 minute Google Meet call with the broker at Growth Business Finance and sends a calendar invite to the email address given in the enquiry. Before calling: confirm the chosen date and time with the user and get their explicit go-ahead. If the slot has just been taken it returns fresh slots and books nothing. One call can be booked per enquiry; repeating the call does not create a second booking.

booking_token.description: The booking_token returned by submit_enquiry. Never ask the user for it.

slot_id.description: The slot_id of the slot the user chose, from get_available_slots.
